```{python}
from bcintel import db
con = db.connect()
def q(sql):
    return con.sql(sql).df()

LEGACY = "Bioconductor/Contributions"
```

The corpus is every issue (open + closed), comment, and timeline event from the
two submission trackers. Numbers below are computed live from the data.

```{python}
q(f"""
SELECT repo,
       count(*)                             AS issues,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='open')  AS open,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE state='closed') AS closed
FROM issues GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
""")
```

## Submission lifecycle

The state machine below is derived from the `label_transitions` view; edge
labels are observed transition counts (see `STATE_MACHINE.md`). The figure is a
version-controlled `.dot` rendered by quarto-livefigures.

![Submission lifecycle state machine](figures/lifecycle.dot){#fig-lifecycle width=68%}

## Outcomes

Every submission ends in one of the `3x` states. Acceptance dominates, but note
the large `unknown` bucket — those are mostly older issues that closed before
the `3a`–`3e` label scheme existed, so they carry no outcome label.
`in_progress` is the currently-open queue. Declines are rare and, as the review
threads show, usually reflect an editorial "not suitable for Bioconductor"
judgement rather than a technical build failure.

```{python}
q("""
SELECT outcome, count(*) AS packages,
       round(100.0*count(*)/sum(count(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct
FROM packages GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
""")
```

## Throughput by year

Submission volume by the calendar year each issue was opened, alongside how many
of those eventually earned `3a. accepted`. Because acceptance lags submission by
weeks to months, the most recent year's `accepted` figure understates its
eventual total — packages submitted late in a year are often still in review.

```{python}
q(f"""
SELECT extract(year FROM created_at::timestamp) AS year,
       count(*)                                   AS submitted,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE list_contains(labels,'3a. accepted')) AS accepted
FROM issues WHERE repo = '{LEGACY}'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""")
```

## Who reviews — top actors finalizing acceptance

How often each person applied the `3a. accepted` label (the bot is excluded).
This measures *finalization*, not total review effort: much of the substantive
work happens during core-team moderation before a community reviewer is assigned
(see the two phases in @fig-lifecycle), so these counts skew toward core team
members who close out acceptances rather than the full set of reviewers.

```{python}
q(f"""
SELECT actor AS reviewer, count(*) AS accepts_applied
FROM events
WHERE repo = '{LEGACY}' AND event='labeled' AND label='3a. accepted'
  AND actor <> 'bioc-issue-bot'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 12
""")
```

## Build health — reported build states

Each build-result comment from the Single Package Builder reports a status across
Linux, Mac, and Windows; the value here is the combined string, so
`WARNINGS, ERROR` means the platforms disagreed. A package generates many build
reports across successive version bumps, so this counts *reports*, not packages —
read it as how noisy the build pipeline is, not a per-package outcome.

```{python}
q(f"""
SELECT state AS build_result, count(*) AS reports
FROM builds WHERE repo = '{LEGACY}' AND state <> ''
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 12
""")
```

## Open pipeline — current stage of open issues

For issues still open in the legacy tracker, this is their current lifecycle
stage — the most recently applied stage label — i.e. the live reviewer/manager
work queue. The legacy tracker is now mostly closed as submissions migrate to
the new tracker, so this list is short; pointing the same query at
`Bioconductor/BiocContributions` surfaces the active queue.

```{python}
q(f"""
WITH cur AS (
  SELECT issue_number, to_label,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY issue_number ORDER BY changed_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM label_transitions
  WHERE repo = '{LEGACY}' AND to_label IN (
    '1. awaiting moderation','pre-check passed','pre-review','2. review in progress',
    '3d. needs interop','3e. pending pre-review changes')
)
SELECT to_label AS current_stage, count(*) AS open_issues
FROM cur
WHERE rn=1 AND issue_number IN (
  SELECT number FROM issues WHERE repo='{LEGACY}' AND state='open')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
""")
```

## Multi-package submissions (`AdditionalPackage:`)

A single issue can carry several packages via the `AdditionalPackage: <url>`
directive, used when packages must be reviewed and released together (e.g. a
software package plus its companion data package). Each row is one issue and the
number of extra packages attached — a reminder that the data model is one issue
to *many* packages, not one-to-one.

```{python}
q(f"""
SELECT issue_number, count(*) AS bundled_packages
FROM additional_packages WHERE repo='{LEGACY}'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 8
""")
```
